sentences.text: QSM processing was performed using QSMbly (Stewart, 2026).
Inhomogeneity correction (Eckstein et al., 2019) was applied to the RSS-combined magnitude image.

A brain mask was generated using Otsu thresholding (Otsu, 1979) of the ROMEO phase quality map (computed from phase data and the inhomogeneity-corrected RSS-combined magnitude), followed by dilation, hole-filling, and erosion.
Phase offset removal was performed using the HIP method (Eckstein et al., 2018).
Phase unwrapping was performed using ROMEO (Dymerska et al., 2021).
The B0 field map was estimated as a weighted average of the unwrapped echo phases.
Background field removal was performed using V-SHARP (Wu et al., 2012).

The V-SHARP background was estimated on an isotropic grid: the field and mask were cropped to the brain mask's bounding box and resampled trilinearly, and the background field estimated there was interpolated back to the acquired grid, so the local field kept the acquired resolution.
Dipole inversion was performed using iLSQR (Li et al., 2015).
Susceptibility values were referenced to the mean susceptibility within the reconstruction mask (the brain mask less any rim eroded by background field removal).
Background field removal was performed using V-SHARP (Wu et al., 2012) with SMV kernel radii from 10 to 2 mm in 1 mm steps.
Background field removal was performed using V-SHARP (Wu et al., 2012) with SMV kernel radii from 12 to 0 mm in 1 mm steps.
Background field removal was performed using V-SHARP (Wu et al., 2012) with SMV kernel radii from 12 to 3 mm in 1 mm steps.
Background field removal was performed using PDF (Liu et al., 2011).
Background field removal was performed using LBV (Zhou et al., 2014).
Background field removal was performed using LBV (Zhou et al., 2014) with depth = 3, peel = 1, n1 = 20, n2 = 80, n3 = 90, and precision = single.
Background field removal was performed using LBV (Zhou et al., 2014) with tolerance = 0.000001.
Dipole inversion was performed using TKD (Thresholded K-space Division) (Shmueli et al., 2009).
Dipole inversion was performed using TKD (Thresholded K-space Division) (Shmueli et al., 2009) with threshold = 0.
Dipole inversion was performed using xQSM (deep-learning dipole inversion) (Gao et al., 2021).
Network inference was run on overlapping tiles (tile size 56 voxels, halo 4 voxels).
Dipole inversion was performed using QSMnetME (deep-learning dipole inversion) (Kim et al., 2025).

QSM was computed using the Total Generalized Variation (TGV) algorithm (Langkammer et al., 2015), with background field removal and dipole inversion performed jointly. For single-echo data TGV was applied to the wrapped phase of the echo and also performed the phase unwrapping; for multi-echo data TGV was applied to the B0 field map, computed as described below, expressed as phase at the first echo time. The regularisation weights are in radians at that echo time and the field strength, and the susceptibility was converted to ppm with them.

QSM was computed using QSMART (Yaghmaie et al., 2021), with spatially dependent filtering for background field removal, iLSQR dipole inversion (Li et al., 2015), and Frangi vesselness-based tissue/vasculature separation.
Vessels were detected on the mean magnitude over echoes, bias-corrected with N4 (Tustison et al., 2010).

Dipole inversion was performed using MEDI (Morphology Enabled Dipole Inversion) (Liu et al., 2011), with the local field high-passed by a 5 mm spherical mean value (SMV) filter within the mask shrunk by that radius.
MEDI's zero reference to the ventricular CSF (MEDI+0; Liu et al., 2018) was applied to runs of at least three echoes.
Dipole inversion was performed using MEDI (Morphology Enabled Dipole Inversion) (Liu et al., 2011), with maximum spherical mean value (mSMV) filtering of the local field (Roberts et al., 2024).

Dipole inversion was performed using STAR-QSM (Streaking Artifact Reduction) (Wei et al., 2015) with zero-padding of 8 × 8 × 20 voxels per side and the field converted to phase at the sum of the echo times.

Dipole inversion was performed using STAR-QSM (Streaking Artifact Reduction) (Wei et al., 2015) with zero-padding of 8 × 8 × 20 voxels per side and the field converted to phase at an echo time of 20 ms.
Dipole inversion was performed using NLTV (Nonlinear Total Variation) (Milovic et al., 2018) with the field converted to phase at the last echo time.

The B0 field map was estimated by a magnitude-weighted nonlinear fit of the complex echo signal (Fit_ppm_complex, MEDI toolbox; Liu et al., 2013); the fitted phase per echo spacing was unwrapped using ROMEO (Dymerska et al., 2021) and divided by the echo spacing.
MRI processing was performed using QSMbly (Stewart, 2026).
Inhomogeneity correction (Eckstein et al., 2019) was applied to the RSS-combined magnitude image.

A brain mask was generated using Otsu thresholding (Otsu, 1979) of the ROMEO phase quality map (computed from phase data and the inhomogeneity-corrected RSS-combined magnitude), followed by dilation, hole-filling, and erosion.
Phase unwrapping was performed separately for each echo using the Laplacian method (Schofield & Zhu, 2003).
Phase unwrapping was performed separately for each echo using PRELUDE (Jenkinson, 2003).
Phase unwrapping was performed separately for each echo using PRELUDE (Jenkinson, 2003) with 6 phase partitions and regions labelled slice by slice.
Phase unwrapping was performed separately for each echo using PRELUDE (Jenkinson, 2003) with 0 phase partitions.
Phase unwrapping was performed separately for each echo using MEDI's magnitude-guided region growing (Liu et al., 2013).
Before any other processing, each echo's complex image was multiplied in k-space by a Tukey window with a taper ratio of 0.4.

Before field mapping, in runs with more than one echo and magnitude images, every echo was rigidly co-registered to the first echo by maximising the normalised cross-correlation of the magnitude images over a multi-resolution pyramid, and the phase was resampled with it through the complex signal; the brain mask was restricted to voxels covered by every echo.
R2* maps were computed from multi-echo magnitude data using the ARLO method (Pei et al., 2015).
Paramagnetic and diamagnetic susceptibility maps were computed using R2*-QSM susceptibility source separation (Dimov et al., 2022) within the reconstruction mask.
Paramagnetic and diamagnetic susceptibility maps were computed using DECOMPOSE-QSM (Chen et al., 2021) within the reconstruction mask.
The same susceptibility map was used for the signal phase at every echo.
R2 maps were fitted from multi-echo spin-echo magnitude data using an Extended Phase Graph dictionary (Weigel, 2015).
R2' was computed as R2* - R2 where a multi-echo spin-echo acquisition was available, and otherwise, at 3 T only, estimated from R2* with R2PRIMEnet (Kim et al., 2025; patch = 128 × 128 × 64 voxels).
Negative R2' values were set to zero.
Paramagnetic and diamagnetic susceptibility maps were computed using χ-separation (iLSQR) (Shin et al., 2021) within the reconstruction mask.
The two sources were initialised from the susceptibility map and solved by LSQR, streaking removal and a non-negative refinement.
The susceptibility map separated was reconstructed from the local field by iLSQR (Li et al., 2015).
Paramagnetic and diamagnetic susceptibility maps were computed using χ-separation (MEDI) (Shin et al., 2021) within the reconstruction mask.

The two sources were initialised from the susceptibility map, the data terms were weighted by a noise map from the echo magnitudes, and the susceptibility within a CSF mask from ARLO R2* (Pei et al., 2015) was regularised towards uniformity.
Paramagnetic and diamagnetic susceptibility maps were computed using WaveSep (Fang et al., 2023) within the reconstruction mask.
Paramagnetic and diamagnetic susceptibility maps were computed using hollow-cylinder χ-separation (HC-ChiSep) (Stewart et al., 2026) within the reconstruction mask.

Paramagnetic and diamagnetic susceptibility maps were computed using SUSEP-Net (deep-learning source separation) (Li et al., 2025) within the reconstruction mask, with the network applied as a sliding window of 96×96×64-voxel patches.
Negative χ+ and |χ−| values were set to zero.

Paramagnetic and diamagnetic susceptibility maps were computed using χ-sepnet (deep-learning source separation) (Kim et al., 2025) within the reconstruction mask, with the inputs resampled to 1 mm with B0 along z and the susceptibility channel computed by QSMnetME, as in the χ-separation toolbox, and the maps resampled back and the networks applied as a sliding window of 128×128×64-voxel patches.

χ-separation used R2' measured as R2* - R2 where a multi-echo spin-echo acquisition was available, and otherwise its own R2', estimated from R2* with R2PRIMEnet (Kim et al., 2025) in the network's training frame.
Paramagnetic and diamagnetic susceptibility maps were computed using DECOMPOSE-QSM (Chen et al., 2021) within the reconstruction mask, with χ bound = 0.3 ppm.
The χ search was bounded from the field strength and echo spacing.

Paramagnetic and diamagnetic susceptibility maps were computed using χ-sepnet (deep-learning source separation) (Kim et al., 2025) within the reconstruction mask, with the network applied on the acquired grid to this run's QSM and 128×128×64-voxel sliding-window patches.

Paramagnetic and diamagnetic susceptibility maps were computed using χ-sepnet (deep-learning source separation) (Kim et al., 2025) within the reconstruction mask, with the network applied on the acquired grid to this run's QSM and 128×128×96-voxel sliding-window patches.

Paramagnetic and diamagnetic susceptibility maps were computed using χ-sepnet (deep-learning source separation) (Kim et al., 2025) within the reconstruction mask, with the inputs resampled to 1 mm with B0 along z and the susceptibility channel computed by QSMnetME, as in the χ-separation toolbox, and the maps resampled back.

Paramagnetic and diamagnetic susceptibility maps were computed using χ-sepnet (deep-learning source separation) (Kim et al., 2025) within the reconstruction mask, with the inputs resampled to 1 mm with B0 along z and the susceptibility channel computed by QSMnetME, as in the χ-separation toolbox, and the maps resampled back and the networks applied as a sliding window of 128×128×96-voxel patches.
Where R2' was estimated, the R2' map in the outputs was not an input to χ-separation.

Paramagnetic and diamagnetic susceptibility maps were computed using χ-sepnet (deep-learning source separation) (Kim et al., 2025) within the reconstruction mask, with the inputs resampled to 1 mm with B0 along z and the susceptibility channel computed by QSMnetME, as in the χ-separation toolbox, and the maps resampled back and the networks applied as a sliding window of 100×128×64-voxel patches.

Paramagnetic and diamagnetic susceptibility maps were computed using χ-sepnet (deep-learning source separation) (Kim et al., 2025) within the reconstruction mask, with the network applied on the acquired grid to this run's QSM and 100×128×64-voxel sliding-window patches.

The B0 field map was estimated by a magnitude-weighted nonlinear fit of the complex echo signal (Fit_ppm_complex, MEDI toolbox; Liu et al., 2013); the fitted phase per echo spacing was unwrapped using the Laplacian method (Schofield & Zhu, 2003) and divided by the echo spacing.
Dipole inversion was performed using FANSI (Nonlinear TV) (Milovic et al., 2018).
Susceptibility-weighted images were computed with CLEAR-SWI (Eckstein et al., 2021). Minimum-intensity projections of these images were also computed.
Susceptibility-weighted images were computed with CLEAR-SWI (Eckstein et al., 2021). Minimum-intensity projections of these images were also computed.

Susceptibility map-weighted images were computed (Gho et al., 2014) by weighting the magnitude with a mask derived from the susceptibility map, separately for paramagnetic and diamagnetic sources, each followed by a minimum-intensity projection.
T2* and R2* maps were computed from multi-echo magnitude data using the ARLO method (Pei et al., 2015).

Susceptibility-weighted images were computed with CLEAR-SWI (Eckstein et al., 2021) using ROMEO phase unwrapping (Dymerska et al., 2021). Minimum-intensity projections of these images were also computed.

The brain was parcellated from the GRE magnitude using SynthSeg v1 (Billot et al., 2023), yielding 32 FreeSurfer-labelled structures, with the network applied as a sliding window of 96×96×96-voxel patches overlapping by at least half a patch, their posteriors Gaussian-weighted.

Each quantitative map was then summarised within every segmented structure (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum and 5th/95th percentiles over the structure's voxels), excluding voxels the map does not cover.

Susceptibility values were referenced to the mean susceptibility in the thalamus (SynthSeg label), computed within the reconstruction mask (the brain mask less any rim eroded by background field removal).

Susceptibility values were referenced to the mean susceptibility in the thalamus ('qsmbly' segmentation label), computed within the reconstruction mask (the brain mask less any rim eroded by background field removal).
A brain mask was generated using BET brain extraction (Smith, 2002) of the inhomogeneity-corrected RSS-combined magnitude image, followed by erosion (2 iterations).

A brain mask was generated using Otsu thresholding (Otsu, 1979) of the ROMEO phase quality map (computed from phase data and the inhomogeneity-corrected RSS-combined magnitude), followed by dilation, hole-filling, and erosion (0 iterations).

A brain mask was generated using Otsu thresholding (Otsu, 1979) of the ROMEO phase quality map (computed from phase data and the inhomogeneity-corrected RSS-combined magnitude), followed by dilation, hole-filling, and erosion (3 iterations).
Background field removal was performed using V-SHARP (Wu et al., 2012).

The V-SHARP background was estimated on an isotropic grid: the field and mask were cropped to the brain mask's bounding box and resampled trilinearly, and the background field estimated there was interpolated back to the acquired grid, so the local field kept the acquired resolution.
Dipole inversion was performed using iLSQR (Li et al., 2015).

Two-pass artefact reduction (Stewart et al., 2022) was applied: background field removal and dipole inversion were repeated against a second mask generated using Otsu thresholding (Otsu, 1979) of the ROMEO phase quality map (computed from phase data and the inhomogeneity-corrected RSS-combined magnitude), whose holes around strong susceptibility sources were left unfilled, and the two susceptibility maps were combined by taking the second reconstruction wherever it was defined and the first elsewhere.
Susceptibility values were referenced to the mean susceptibility within the reconstruction mask (the brain mask less any rim eroded by background field removal).
N4 inhomogeneity correction (Tustison et al., 2010) was applied to the RSS-combined magnitude image.
N4 inhomogeneity correction (Tustison et al., 2010; at most 50 and 40 iterations at 2 fitting levels) was applied to the RSS-combined magnitude image.

Before field mapping, in runs with more than one echo and magnitude images, every echo was rigidly co-registered to the first echo by maximising the normalised cross-correlation of the magnitude images over a multi-resolution pyramid, and the phase was resampled with it through the complex signal; the brain mask was restricted to voxels covered by every echo.
